sections.heading: The Serving Problem
sections.body: You've got a 70 billion parameter model. Now serve it to a thousand users. That's the trillion-dollar question — and two tools have very different answers.

sections.heading: How vLLM Works
sections.body: Built at UC Berkeley, vLLM uses PagedAttention — it treats GPU memory like virtual memory pages. No fragmentation, no waste, maximum batch throughput.

sections.heading: vLLM by the Numbers
sections.body: Pure throughput domination on GPU hardware.

sections.heading: How llama.cpp Works
sections.body: Georgi Gerganov rewrote LLM inference in pure C/C++ — no Python, no CUDA required. It quantizes models from 16-bit down to 4-bit, letting you run 70B models on a MacBook.
bulletPoints: GGUF format: quantized model files (Q4, Q5, Q8)
Runs on Raspberry Pi to server racks

sections.heading: The Real Trade-off
sections.body: It's not about which is better — it's about what you're optimizing for.

right.label: llama.cpp
points: Runs on CPU, Mac, edge devices

sections.heading: Setup: Two Commands
sections.body: Getting started with either takes minutes, not hours.

codeSnippet.code:
# vLLM — GPU serving in 2 lines
pip install vllm
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2

# llama.cpp — CPU/Metal inference
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
cmake -B build && cmake --build build
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m models/llama-3.1-70b-q4_k_m.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

sections.heading: The .safetensor Question
sections.body: vLLM loads models in safetensors format — full precision weights stored in a safe, memory-mapped binary. It's fast to load but needs serious VRAM.
bulletPoints: vLLM trades disk space for raw throughput speed
llama.cpp trades speed for fitting bigger models

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.body: Both projects launched within months of each other.

events.label: llama.cpp: C++ inference, no GPU needed

sections.heading: When to Use What
sections.body: Pick your weapon based on your deployment reality.
bulletPoints: vLLM: production APIs with hundreds of concurrent users
vLLM: you have NVIDIA GPUs and .safetensor models
llama.cpp: edge devices, MacBooks, limited VRAM
llama.cpp: you need to serve a model bigger than your GPU
Both: they solve different problems — not competitors
